desc:
The array nums holds positive integers in strictly increasing order. Imagine writing down the positive integers 1, 2, 3, ... and crossing out every value that occurs in nums. Return the k-th integer that is not crossed out.

Example: for nums = [2, 3, 4, 7, 11] the missing positive integers are 1, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, ..., so for k = 5 the answer is 9. A solution faster than counting one integer at a time exists.
hints: Walking through the positive integers one by one and skipping those in the array works when k is small, but k can be a billion.
At index i there are exactly nums[i] - (i + 1) missing positive integers smaller than nums[i]. This count never decreases as i grows.
Binary search the first index idx whose missing count is at least k (use n if there is none). The answer is then idx + k.
editorial: Let miss(i) = nums[i] - i - 1, the number of absent positive integers below nums[i]. Because the array is strictly increasing, miss is non-decreasing, so it can be binary searched.

Find the smallest index idx with miss(idx) ≥ k, or n if no index qualifies. Then exactly idx array elements lie below the answer, so the answer is the k-th integer after skipping those idx values: idx + k. This also covers the case where the answer lies beyond the last element.
Time is O(log n) after reading the input, space O(1). The answer is at most 109 + 104, which fits in a 32-bit integer.
